title: Save the Cat!
summary: Blake Snyder's 15-beat structure for feature screenplays. Page numbers assume a ~110-page screenplay.

beats.label: Opening Image
beats.summary: A snapshot that captures tone, mood, type, and scope of the film, and establishes the protagonist's starting point.

beats.label: Theme Stated
beats.summary: Someone (usually not the hero) poses a question or makes a statement that is the theme of the movie.

beats.label: Set-Up
beats.summary: The protagonist's world before the catalyst. Establishes the status quo and the protagonist's flaws.

beats.label: Catalyst
beats.summary: The inciting incident. Life-changing event that sets the story in motion.

beats.label: Debate
beats.summary: The protagonist debates whether to take action. Doubts, fears, second thoughts.

beats.label: Break Into Two
beats.summary: The protagonist makes a decisive choice and crosses into Act Two — the upside-down world.

beats.label: B Story
beats.summary: A new character or storyline appears, often a love interest. The B story carries the theme.

beats.label: Fun and Games
beats.summary: The promise of the premise. The 'trailer moments' — what the audience came to see.

beats.label: Midpoint
beats.summary: A false victory or false defeat. The stakes are raised and the protagonist's quest pivots.

beats.label: Bad Guys Close In
beats.summary: External and internal pressure mounts. The protagonist's plan starts to fall apart.

beats.label: All Is Lost
beats.summary: The opposite of the midpoint. The lowest moment. Often a 'whiff of death' — a literal or symbolic loss.

beats.label: Dark Night of the Soul
beats.summary: The protagonist hits rock bottom and must dig deep to find a new approach.

beats.label: Break Into Three
beats.summary: The protagonist finds the answer — usually by synthesizing the A and B stories — and resolves to act.

beats.label: Finale
beats.summary: Act Three. The protagonist executes the new plan, defeats the antagonist, and changes the world.

beats.label: Final Image
beats.summary: The mirror of the opening image. Shows how much the protagonist (and world) has changed.
